legend: Well-differentiated leiomyosarcoma. The tumour is composed of fascicles of spindle cells with abundant bright eosinophilic cytoplasm; the nuclei are ovoid with blunt ends, mild pleomorphism, and occasional mitotic activity.
Moderately differentiated leiomyosarcoma. The tumour has an increased N:C ratio, moderate nuclear pleomorphism, and conspicuous mitotic activity.
Poorly differentiated leiomyosarcoma. The tumour has a morphology resembling an undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma, juxtaposed with an area of more differentiated tumour.

Poorly differentiated leiomyosarcoma showing loss of immunoreactivity for h-caldesmon. A similar pattern was also observed for desmin, while SMA in this case was retained throughout the tumour (h-caldesmon).
Dedifferentiated leiomyosarcoma with areas of osteoid-like matrix. Elsewhere, this tumour contained regions with a conventional morphology and immunophenotype.
Leiomyosarcoma arising in a patient with Li–Fraumeni syndrome. This tumour contained areas with a vague storiform pattern (H&E).
An area of prominent myxoid stroma.
An area of prominent stromal hyalinization. Note: this change is arising in the absence of any prior therapy.
Leiomyosarcoma with an abrupt transition to necrosis (H&E).
Leiomyosarcoma containing an area with prominent osteoclast-type giant cells (H&E).
Contrast-enhanced CT, in the coronal and axial planes, showing an enhancing mass arising exophytically from the infrarenal inferior vena cava (arrows).
